answer: A memory-hardness protocol requires each agent to compute a rapid spiral traversal across a multi-gigabyte buffer. To avoid a centralized walled garden, verification nodes bridge challenge nonces directly to agents under strict latency deadlines. Because this access pattern defeats cache prefetching, an attacker must dedicate physical RAM per identity, incurring linear hardware costs. However, transient memory bus contention can delay honest agents, causing false rejections.
